column1: # steps.tsv — THE process of installing this profile, declared ONCE, in run order.
#   D1. The precedent is questions.tsv (2026-09-23, D6): a seam is a ROW, and
#   more than one command reads the same rows. Here the fact being declared is
#   not a question but a STEP, and the reason it had to become data is measured:
#   a phase was one linear bash function, a mid-function `return 1` abandoned
#   every later step in it, and NOTHING wrote that down. `app` has fourteen
#   steps; its mint-key step returned on failure and silently skipped nine .env
#   writes and the cockpit build, and `./setup.sh boot` after it was accepted.
#   The phase FUNCTIONS stay. This file does not turn 3,200 lines of bash into a
#   step interpreter — it makes the existing phases ACCOUNTABLE: the driver runs
#   phase_<name> as before, then runs every row's `probe`. A phase is DONE only
#   when every one of its rows probes true, and a phase that returns 0 with a row
#   probing false is a FAIL naming the row. That is what turns "the step after
#   the one that failed never ran" from invisible into a line.
#   COLUMNS, tab-separated, `-` where a field is empty:
#     phase      check | machine | fetch | llm | stack | app | verify | test |
#                boot | demo — the driver's order, and the only phases there are
#     step       the step's name, which is the PASS/FAIL check-name the phase
#                already prints. The ledger keys on `<phase>/<step>`, so the
#                same name may appear in two phases (venv, cockpit,
#                image-sandbox, embed-dimension each do) without colliding
#     kind       run    = the phase function executes it
#                gate   = the driver STOPS here until a human has acted (exit
#                         3); the row's `probe` is how it knows they have
#                human  = never executed by the driver; a thing the operator
#                         does in a UI, recorded once its probe passes
#     requires   comma-separated `<phase>/<step>` that must be DONE first.
#                Backward-only and acyclic — an earlier phase, or an earlier row
#                of this one. The driver refuses a phase whose requires are not
#                done and names the first one (D2's rule 1)
#     reads      the .env keys whose VALUES are this step's inputs. They are
#                FINGERPRINTED (sha256 over KEY=VALUE in this order), so an
#                .env edit re-runs exactly the steps it changed and nothing
#                else. Named keys only — never a glob, which has no stable order
#     writes     every .env key and state artifact this step is the ONLY writer
#                of. A key written outside this column is the v2.52.0 "eight
#                blank Systems links nobody types" bug, and v2.48.0's missing
#                CC_LLM_BASE_URL before it, so the rule is enforced:
#                tests/test_single_steps_schema.py fails the suite when a
#                set_kv / set_kv_if_unset target in deploy/single/*.sh is absent
#                here, or appears twice. `CC_IMG_*` is the one family (the
#                resolver writes one line per image); lower-case entries are
#                state-dir or build artifacts, not answers
#     probe      a bash function in setup.sh: exit 0 = the step's effect is
#                PRESENT NOW. Three rules it lives under — it may not mutate
#                anything (the same walker that keeps `check` dry is run over
#                every probe), it may not spend a token or a minute (the ledger's
#                version + fingerprint is what records that the real round trip
#                was made, which is why probe-chat reads the catalog rather than
#                asking for another completion), and a step that cannot apply is
#                DONE — an off flag returns 0, because "not applicable" is not
#     doc        one plain sentence, for the generated checklist (D8, P4)
#   Rows are in RUN order, and the driver walks them in it.

column8: doc
Prove this deployment still matches the release it claims to be, before anything is changed.
Reach the podman machine over ssh (a no-op on bare Linux, where there is none).
Have the machine import this host's trust store at every start.
Install CC_CA_BUNDLE as a trust anchor inside the machine and rebuild its trust store.
Prove from INSIDE the machine that a registry's certificate now verifies.
Write the machine's registries drop-in from the mirror seams.
Write the machine's containers.conf proxy drop-in from CC_PROXY.
Resolve every images.txt row against the registry that will serve it and write the refs into .env.
Pull the spine's Postgres image.
Pull the knowledge graph's Neo4j image.
Pull the Redis image LiteLLM caches through.
Pull the LiteLLM proxy image.
Pull the n8n image, when CC_ENABLE_N8N=1.
Pull the base image the Graphiti MCP image is built from.
Pull the base image the sandbox image is built from, when CC_ENABLE_SANDBOX=1.
Pull the base image the crawler image is built from, when CC_ENABLE_CRAWLER=1.
Pull the bundled speech engine's image, when CC_ENABLE_SPEECH=1.
Build the Graphiti MCP image against your sources.
Build the agent sandbox image, when CC_ENABLE_SANDBOX=1.
Build the browser-rendering crawl image, when CC_ENABLE_CRAWLER=1.
Create the install's CPython 3.12 virtual environment and resolve the Python graph.
Install the cockpit's npm tree from the configured registry.
Generate every credential .env still leaves blank (it never overwrites one that is set).
Bring the LiteLLM proxy up with its own database and redis.
Wait for the proxy to finish its first-boot migrations and answer /health/liveliness.
Start the bundled speech engine, when CC_ENABLE_SPEECH=1.
Say which way this install answers the LLM question: declared in .env, or entered in the LiteLLM UI.
Register every alias this deployment requires, as a real row or as a skeleton.
YOUR MOVE, unless .env declared the upstream: fill in each alias's provider in the LiteLLM UI at http://127.0.0.1:<CC_LITELLM_PORT>/ui.
Get a real completion back through the cc-default alias — the one the agents address.
Get schema-constrained JSON back through graphiti-llm, which is what graph extraction needs.
Get a completion back through gpt-4.1-nano, the alias graphiti_core addresses by that literal name.
Wait for the speech engine to answer /health, when CC_ENABLE_SPEECH=1.
Install the TTS and STT model snapshots into the engine's volume (the first call downloads them).
Synthesise speech through the cc-tts alias, when CC_ENABLE_SPEECH=1.
Transcribe what cc-tts just said through the cc-stt alias, when CC_ENABLE_SPEECH=1.
Get a vector back through the cc-embedding alias.
Record the MEASURED embedding dimension in .env — it is permanent once the graph index exists.
Assert the sandbox image is in local storage rather than building one mid-deploy.
Assert the crawler image is in local storage rather than building one mid-deploy.
Refuse to create the graph before the embedding dimension has been measured.
Bring the whole stack up and wait on compose.yaml's healthchecks.
Make the containers come back after a host reboot (podman-restart inside the machine).
Assert the virtual environment the app runs in.
Install central_command editable into that environment.
Assert the one answer file and its mode (0600 where the filesystem honours it).
Mint the spine's OWN LiteLLM virtual key, so a leak of the agents' credential cannot reconfigure the proxy.
Derive the proxy URL the app dials.
Derive which model the agents run on (this profile's proxy carries cc-default).
Derive the alias the graph writer embeds through.
Derive the connection string for LiteLLM's own database.
Derive the Systems page's link to the proxy UI.
Derive the Systems page's link to the Neo4j browser.
Derive the Systems page's link to n8n, when CC_ENABLE_N8N=1.
Derive the Systems page's link to the crawl service, when CC_ENABLE_CRAWLER=1.
Derive the Systems page's link to the sandbox runner, when CC_ENABLE_SANDBOX=1.
Build the cockpit — both the SPA and the Node server every panel routes through.
Assert every deployment and configuration fact verify.sh knows, under the admin key.
Assert the same deployment LIVE: a real completion and the embedding dimension.
Run the offline suite — the gate, once per release.
YOUR MOVE: tell the agents what to call you — setup asks on a terminal, the cockpit asks on first run otherwise.
Start the API detached and wait for /health.
Assert first boot hired the founding roster.
Start the cockpit server detached and wait for it to answer.
Register the logon entry that brings the two host processes back after a reboot (Windows only).
Enrol the fixture email (a repeat Message-ID is a no-op by design).
Let the dispatcher claim it and run a real triage against your endpoint.
YOUR MOVE: open the cockpit's Decisions Inbox, read the proposal and its evidence, and decide.
Assert the decision reached the event log.
Assert the Executor performed the approved action and stamped provenance.
